source_text: Quis tu es, qui oestro Marcionis concitatus in excidium aequitatis irrumpas? Qui sub censuram linguae tuae mysteriis adhuc Manichaeorum lubricae Dei tam iudicia quam praecepta compellas? Nemo hoc umquam facere, nisi qui prius ea negavit, aggressus est. Tu testamentum Dei, quod ratio aequitas pietas veritas fide scribentibus Prophetis quasi quidam sacrorum testium ordo signavit, audebis Manichaeo auctore perrumpere. Olim et intellegentiae sanctitatem et religionis speciem perdidisti, si hac sententia, quae apud Ezechielem est, traducis tuae putes aut auxilium reperiri aut exitium non teneri.
pass_a_gloss: Who are you, who stirred by the gadfly of Marcion burst into the destruction of fairness? Who under the censure of your tongue still slippery from the mysteries of the Manichaeans compel both the judgments and the precepts of God? No one has ever attempted to do this except who first denied them. Will you dare, with the Manichaean as author, to break through the testament of God, which reason, fairness, piety, truth sealed for the Prophets writing in faith as a certain order of sacred witnesses? Long ago you have lost both the holiness of intelligence and the appearance of religion, if by this sentence which is in Ezekiel you think either help for your vine-layer is found or its destruction is not held.

lemmas.lexica: LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: Who are you, rushing to destroy fairness under the impulse of Marcion’s frenzy? Who are you, forcing both God’s judgments and his commands under the censorship of your tongue, still slippery from Manichaean mysteries? No one ever attempted this without first rejecting them. Will you dare, with Mani as your authority, to break God’s testament, which reason, fairness, devotion, and truth—as though a line of sacred witnesses—sealed through the prophets writing faithfully? You long ago lost both purity of understanding and the appearance of religion if you think the pronouncement in Ezekiel either offers support for your inherited sin or fails to contain its destruction.

choices.why: Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Explicitly discusses the prophet’s pronouncement on personal righteousness and guilt rather than inherited guilt.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
